text:
Fixed. Both balancers now return nil instead of panicking when the target list is empty:
- middleware/proxy.go: randomBalancer.Next returns nil when len(targets) == 0 (before calling rand.Intn), and roundRobinBalancer.Next returns nil when len(targets) == 0 (before the modulo, which was the divide-by-zero). The round-robin Next now also takes the read lock like the random one, so it no longer races with AddTarget/RemoveTarget.
Verified: NewRandomBalancer(nil).Next(c) -> nil, NewRoundRobinBalancer([]*ProxyTarget{}).Next(c) -> nil, and after AddTarget/RemoveTarget the normal random/round-robin behavior is unchanged. Full pre-existing test suite still passes (go test ./...).

Fixed. Router.Find no longer seeds the context path with the requested URL: it starts with an empty path and only sets c.path to the matched route's registered path (router.go). So for a request that matches no route, c.Path() is "" (e.g. in HTTPErrorHandler), while matched routes still report their registered path (e.g. "/users/:id"), and a matched path with a wrong method (405) still reports the route path.
Verified with the snippet from your report plus matched/405 cases; full pre-existing test suite still passes.

Fixed. Context.Scheme() (context.go) now only accepts a real HTTP scheme from the proxy headers: each of X-Forwarded-Proto, X-Forwarded-Protocol and X-Url-Scheme is passed through a new schemeFromHeader helper that returns the first valid `http`/`https` value (case-insensitive, and it skips invalid values in a comma-separated list) or "" otherwise, so an invalid value is ignored and the chain falls through to the next header, defaulting to "http" if none is valid.
Verified: X-Forwarded-Proto: ftp + X-Url-Scheme: https -> "https"; X-Forwarded-Proto: ftp alone -> "http"; valid values and the TLS case unchanged; full pre-existing test suite still passes.
